# Simulated Dataset — Hybrid SQUID Sensor Arrays for Nuclear Plant Radiation Monitoring

**What this is:** a set of NUMERICAL SIMULATION datasets, generated by implementing the
manuscript's own physical equations and quantum-information formalism in Python and
running them (real linear algebra, real statevector simulation, real gradient-descent
circuit training — no hand-typed numbers). It is **not** hardware or field measurement
data. Cite it as "numerical simulation results," the same way the manuscript's own
Sec. 6 ("Numerical Simulations") is meant to be cited.

Master seed: `20260921` (today's date). Every dataset is reproducible by re-running
`run_all.py` with the accompanying `physics.py`, `spectra.py`, `detector.py`, `circuit.py`.

## 3. Data-quality notes on the manuscript itself (please review)

While implementing the manuscript's own formulas exactly as written, three internal
inconsistencies surfaced. These are reported transparently rather than silently
patched, because they affect how the corresponding manuscript equations/figures should
be read:

1. **`eq:ddd`** divides the NRT displacement rate by the atomic number density `n_at`,
   which breaks the dpa (dimensionless) units of the result. We used the standard NRT
   dpa-rate definition (`dpa/s = Φ_n · σ_dpa`, then rescaled by the paper's own arc-dpa
   factor ξ≈0.3) instead.
2. **`κ_TLS` (cm⁻²) multiplying a dimensionless DDD(t)** inside `eq:tls_noise`'s
   `1+κ_TLS·DDD(t)` bracket cannot be dimensionless for any consistent reading of DDD.
   Likewise, **`α_φ` (cm² s⁻¹) multiplied by the raw gamma fluence** (line ~4108) makes
   the radiation-induced dephasing rate exceed the fresh rate within *minutes* at the
   paper's own stated Φ_γ, contradicting its own 5-7 year operational narrative. We kept
   the paper's functional forms (sqrt-growth of 1/f noise with damage; linear growth of
   dephasing rate with fluence) but calibrated the proportionality constants against the
   paper's *own* stated milestones (fresh operating point `NΓ_deph⁰τ_int=8×10⁻³`; the
   implied ~11× 1/f-amplitude growth between the paper's own "fresh" and "pre-failure"
   plotted curves) rather than the literal, unusable coefficients. Full derivation is in
   `physics.py`'s "CALIBRATION NOTE."
3. **Fig. `noise_spectra`'s y-axis** (fΦ₀/√Hz, i.e. values ~1-500×10⁻¹⁵ Φ₀/√Hz) is
   roughly 15-20 orders of magnitude more sensitive than the flux noise implied by the
   paper's own Table B.1 value `A_φ⁽⁰⁾=25 μΦ₀²/Hz` (i.e. μΦ₀/√Hz-scale, the standard
   real-SQUID range). We used the Table B.1 number (the one with actual physical
   provenance / typical real-SQUID magnitude) and report `sqrt(S_Φ)` in μΦ₀/√Hz.

None of this changes the manuscript's qualitative physics claims (noise grows with
damage, GHZ coherence degrades with dose, etc.) — the simulation reproduces those
trends faithfully — but the *absolute* numbers in the current Sec. 6/App. B/C tables and
Fig. 6.1 cannot be derived from the manuscript's own stated equations and constants as
literally typeset, and should be corrected or the discrepancy acknowledged before
submission.

## 4. A genuine (not fabricated) finding worth flagging

We initially implemented the "textbook" version of amplitude encoding — normalize each
spectrum's amplitude vector to unit norm — matching how `fig:quantum_encoding` describes
the encoding. Under that encoding, the quantum relative-entropy detector's AUC was only
**0.60**, far below the classical OC-SVM baseline's **0.95**, because per-sample L2
normalization mathematically erases all information about a spectrum's *overall power*,
and three of the five failure modes (sensor degradation, radiation burst, calibration
drift) manifest mostly as a near-uniform rescaling of the noise floor rather than a
shape change — because, with this SQUID's own stated parameters, the 1/f term dominates
the thermal floor across the *entire* 0.01-1e4 Hz measurement band, so there is no
shape-changing corner-frequency crossover left within the band for those modes to shift.

We addressed this with a magnitude-preserving "ancilla" encoding (255 frequency bins +
1 fixed-reference magnitude ancilla = 2⁸, still exactly n=8 qubits; documented in
`detector.py`/`circuit.py`), after which the quantum detector's AUC rose to **0.95**,
matching the classical baseline. This is included as `04-06` in this dataset. **We
recommend the manuscript state explicitly how magnitude information is preserved (or
isn't) in the amplitude-encoding step**, since the naive reading is a real blind spot.

`coolant_anomaly` remains the hardest mode to detect for *both* detectors (TPR ≈15-34%
at the operating threshold used here) — this matches the manuscript's own Table 6.2,
which also reports it as the lowest-TPR mode, so this qualitative ranking is robust to
the numerical differences described in Section 3 above.

## 5. Scale reductions from the manuscript's stated numbers (compute budget)

| Manuscript | Used here | Why |
|---|---|---|
| M_train = 10,000 | 3,000 (relative-entropy detector) / 200 (VQC sweep) | Eigendecomposition and per-config VQC training cost; 3,000 already gives a converged 256×256 healthy density matrix |
| 10 training seeds (App. C) | 3 seeds | Runtime (8 configs × 3 seeds × 60 parameter-shift iterations ≈ 10 min already) |
| Full statevector VQC training | Same, but 60 iterations, batch size 8 | Parameter-shift needs 2 forward passes per parameter per iteration; kept small enough to run interactively |

AUC is the primary, meaningful metric from the VQC sweep; the reported FAR is computed
at a 95th-percentile threshold *of the same held-out validation set used to set it*, so
it is close to 0.05 by construction for every config and has little power to
discriminate between hyperparameter choices at this validation-set size — treat AUC as
the sweep's real signal, not FAR.

---

## 6. Suggested next steps

- If the manuscript's Sec. 6 tables are meant to report literal QuTiP/PyStan output (as
  Sec. 6.1 states), the parameter inconsistencies in Section 3 above need resolving
  first — the paper's own numbers can't currently be reproduced from its own equations.
- Decide and state explicitly how magnitude information is (or isn't) carried through
  amplitude encoding — see Section 4.
- If a truly full-scale run (M_train=10,000, 10 seeds) is needed for the final
  submission, the same scripts can be re-run with those settings given more compute
  time/budget — everything is parameterized for that.
